chunk_excerpt: The Swin-Transformer (20) model, based on windowing, multi-level feature interaction, and a hierarchical attention mechanism, can simultaneously capture both global and local features in medical images and fuse them together. This model uses convolution operations to segment medical images into small patches and project them into high-dimensional vectors, thereby dividing the feature maps into windows. The feature map vectors undergo sequential processing across four stages. Except for the first stage, which performs linear embedding, the remaining stages first perform patch merging and downsampling on adjacent feature map windows, after which the feature map vectors are fed into a Swin-Transformer block for processing. This experiment uses 224 × 224 × 1 lung medical image feature maps (21); the complete processing workflow and the feature map vectors at each stage are shown in Figure 3.

title: Follow-up imaging after hospital discharge for acute intracerebral hemorrhage in European academic hospitals: a decision-making analysis
chunk_excerpt:
The majority of existent guidelines focus on acute care, but recommendations for follow-up imaging timing, modality, and purpose - detection of rebleeding, hydrocephalus, delayed ischemia, long-term sequelae, recurrence risk stratification - are less standardized. Namely, clinical guidelines from both the European Stroke Organization (ESO) and the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) advocate for the utilization of non-contrast-enhanced computed tomography (NECT) as the initial imaging modality for diagnosing acute ICH [11, 12]. The use of advanced imaging modalities such as CT angiography (CTA), MR-Angiography (MRA), or digital subtraction angiography (DSA) during hospital stay is recommended when clinical or radiological factors suggest potential underlying structural vascular abnormalities [13, 14]. The lack of official recommendations for imaging follow-up after hospital discharge renders decision in clinical practice heterogeneous, furthered by the various constellations that can present such as hemorrhage location, patient age, comorbidities, available imaging modalities and resource allocation.

To address this knowledge gap, the primary aim of this study was to determine how neuroradiology experts approach imaging recommendations after hospital discharge in patients who experienced an ICH, and to subsequently analyze the influence of various clinical factors in the decision-making process.

chunk_excerpt: In addition to network structure innovation, algorithm and component optimization have become important supplementary means to improve model performance in recent years, mainly including loss function optimization, activation function improvement and model interpretability enhancement. In terms of loss function optimization, hybrid loss functions have been proven to effectively solve the problem of medical data category imbalance and optimize classification accuracy (13). In terms of activation function improvement, learnable Piecewise Linear Activation Functions (PLUS) and Activation-Aware Feedforward Networks (AAMLPS) can effectively enhance the model's nonlinear fitting ability, achieving a 0.7% accuracy improvement in medical classification tasks (12). In terms of interpretability optimization, Grad-CAM visualization technology is widely embedded in Transformer backbone networks. It can intuitively display the model's lesion attention area, effectively improving the visual interpretability and diagnostic credibility of the model, and achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 0.97 for tuberculosis auxiliary diagnosis (14). The above studies fully prove that fine-grained optimization of training components and algorithms can effectively improve the comprehensive performance of medical image classification models (15).

title: Multimodal deep learning outperforms clinical and brain region models in predicting stroke-associated pneumonia: an explainable AI study
chunk_excerpt:
With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, deep learning has shown superior performance in medical image analysis by enabling end-to-end feature learning directly from raw imaging data (14). Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), in particular, can automatically learn hierarchical representations that reflect complex anatomical and pathological characteristics. Compared with traditional radiomics approaches, deep learning reduces reliance on manual feature engineering and enables automatic extraction of hierarchical imaging representations from complex medical images (14).

In addition to imaging features, lesion location and brain functional anatomy play critical roles in the development of SAP. Brain regions such as the insular cortex, precentral gyrus, and cingulate cortex are closely associated with swallowing function, respiratory control, and autonomic regulation (15). Damage to these regions may contribute to dysphagia, impaired airway protection, and the induction of stroke-induced immunodepression syndrome (SIDS), thereby increasing the risk of pneumonia (16, 17). These findings align with the emerging concept of the brain–lung axis, and more recently, the brain–gut–lung axis, which posits that central nervous system injury can disrupt systemic immunity and even gut microbiota, ultimately predisposing patients to pulmonary infection (18, 19). Therefore, integrating lesion-aware anatomical information into predictive models may provide additional clinical value.

chunk_excerpt: Early identification of bacterial infection remains challenging because current imaging modalities (e.g., computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging) primarily rely on secondary structural changes associated with infection and inflammation and cannot distinguish between the two. Recent positron emission tomography (PET) imaging approaches targeting human pathogens aim to differentiate live bacteria from mammalian cells [3]. Over the past decade, numerous imaging strategies have taken advantage of bacteria‐specific metabolic pathways, including amino acid incorporation and carbohydrate metabolism [4, 5], folate biosynthesis [6, 7], and siderophore‐mediated iron transport [8]. However, there is no stand‐alone imaging agent for routine differentiation of infection from sterile inflammation in clinical practice, as many candidate PET tracers are limited by short half‐life of carbon‐11 (20.38 min), insufficient specificity, synthetic hurdles, or limited availability of key materials.

Baseline clinical characteristics, including presenting hemorrhage, seizure history, and focal neurological deficits, were obtained from the available medical records.
